title: Clone Graph
keyIdea: Map each original node to its copy. DFS (or BFS): if a node already has a copy, return it; otherwise create the copy, record it in the map first, then copy each neighbour and link it. Every node and edge is copied once, even with cycles.

approaches.name: BFS with a map
approaches.idea: Copy the start node and queue it; pop a node, copy each neighbour the first time it is seen (and queue it), link the copies.
approaches.why: Each node is queued once and each edge is linked once.

approaches.name: DFS with a map
approaches.idea: cloneGraph(node): seen → mp[node]; else make the copy, mp[node] = copy, push_back(cloneGraph(neighbor)) for each neighbour.
approaches.why: Each node is copied once (the map stops repeats); each edge is followed once from each side.

quiz.q: Why put the copy in the map BEFORE cloning the neighbours?
options: A neighbour may lead back to this node (a cycle); it must find the existing copy instead of recursing forever

quiz.q: Why does an already-copied node return mp[node] instead of a new copy?
options: Every edge must point to the single copy of that node
